correctness.rationale: For all finite periodic positive Borel measures with fixed total B, the explicit unique susceptible solution is an integral of convex arc-exponentials divided by constant 1-exp(-delta*T-B); positivity of transmission and separation by arc masses gives strict convexity. The pure pulse solution equals 1-A exp(-delta*t). Its exact impulse-response benefit H(s) is continuous on the period and the global KKT inequality H(s)<=H(0) is equivalent, by full convexity, to unique optimality. On each constant beta season Hprime=delta*C_b exp(delta*s)+b*A exp(-delta*s). The endpoints derivatives are (1-E)(alpha-q*beta_H)/(1-qE) and (1-E)(q*alpha-beta_L)/(1-qE). Their signs force H to decrease throughout the high season and increase throughout the low season; converse sign failure produces strict improvement by a small second pulse. All endpoints, q boundaries, general parameters, and equality cases are addressed. An independent affine-period-map numerical checker confirms exact illustrative values and 54 directional derivatives across 150 randomized parameter families, but finite checks are not offered as proof.

originality.rationale: The new sharp explicit necessary-and-sufficient cutoff separates globally unique pure-pulse optimality from a strict two-pulse improvement for every two-season parameter set. The closest 2026 vaccination paper presents only numerical evidence of the transition near 0.4 and explicitly leaves the upward-jump pulse structure analytically incomplete. The 2026 general optimal-control paper supplies strict convexity and an abstract switching test, but no closed-form two-endpoint cutoff for this weighted susceptibility setting. Earlier pulse SIR results are for different control restrictions. Subsumption risk from an unlocated general theorem remains.

value.rationale: The source identifies an unresolved genuine mathematical/policy question about how upward season jumps lead to pulse vaccination. The new exact parameter-dependent cutoff and exact minimum invasion exposure resolves the pure-pulse phase for the full infinite-dimensional class, replacing a numerical transition near 0.4 by 0.390979957597... for the motivating example. This is not a known-table recomputation or trivial substitution: the endpoint-monotonicity lemma collapses an uncountable set of measure optimality inequalities. The cutoff is of direct use to classify feasible annual vaccine schedules within the given model; it leaves the post-cutoff mixture and nonlinear attack-rate problem open.
